chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"An pregnant woman, whose husband has died, is provided for from the wealth of the child that is in her womb."
Regarding that Muhammad ibn Muslim, the narrator of this hadith, has narrated in agreement with what we presented earlier, he narrated.

key_terms.الَّذِي فِي بَطْنِهَا: That which is in her womb
key_terms.مِنْ مَالِ وَلَدِهَا: From the wealth of her child
key_terms.يُنْفَقُ عَلَيْهَا: She is provided for / maintenance is given to her

ai.seo_question: Who pays for the living expenses of a pregnant widow after her husband's death?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a pregnant widow’s maintenance is drawn from the estate of her unborn child, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the fetus possesses an independent financial status (*māl*) prior to birth. This ensures the mother’s sustenance is secured without depleting the shares of other heirs, a nuance supported by the corroborating narration of Muhammad ibn Muslim.
